Mechanism (cause→failure): No domain randomization on brightness → failure under novel lighting. Policy trained without brightness DR fails almost always on bright/dark lighting, whereas with DR it largely succeeds.
Paper (title, first author, year, arXiv/: Memorize, Adapt, Ignore: Diagnosing Robot Learning…, Zhang et al. 2026 (arXiv:2609.38401)
Task(s) & phase: Cube pick-place; not separated (grasp vs place)
Effect (success w/ vs w/o, trials): Success (Base/Bright/Dark): w/o DR 6/10,1/10,1/10 vs with DR 10/10,8/10,6/10 (10 trials each).

Mechanism (cause→failure): Confounded data variation → poor generalization. When shape and texture vary only together (confounded), policies generalize worse to new objects than when varied independently.
Paper (title, first author, year, arXiv/: Memorize, Adapt, Ignore…, Zhang et al. 2026
Task(s) & phase: “Objects on a scale” (toy pick-place); not separated
Effect (success w/ vs w/o, trials): Test error: Confounded 0.0846 vs Independent 0.0755 on novel categories (point distance). (In-distribution error ~0.0587 vs 0.0605.)

Mechanism (cause→failure): No force-vision curriculum → policy ignores force. Without the FACTR blur schedule, the transformer policy overfits vision and fails to use force (failing to lift or balance objects). With the curriculum, it attends to force.
Intervention (category): Training: Visual blur curriculum (fixed vs decaying)
Paper (title, first author, year, arXiv/: FACTR: Force-Attending Curriculum Training…, Liu et al. 2025 (arXiv:2502.17432)
Task(s) & phase: Multi-object tasks (box lifting, pivoting, etc.); mode switch (contact) phase
Effect (success w/ vs w/o, trials): Pivot task: fixed blur (no curriculum) 16/25 vs with curriculum (e.g. linear) 19/25 success (5 objects×5 trials). (Fig. 9 shows “no FACTR” attention to vision only.)

Mechanism (cause→failure): No temporal memory → fails insertion. Feedforward BC (no history) achieves near-zero success on the Square (nut-on-peg) task, whereas adding a 2-layer LSTM gives nonzero success.
Intervention (category): Architecture: Remove RNN hidden state (BC vs BC-RNN)
Paper (title, first author, year, arXiv/: What Matters in Learning from Offline Human Demonstrations…, Mandlekar et al. 2021 (arXiv:2108.03298)
Task(s) & phase: Square (nut-insertion); failure is at alignment/insert phase (grasp stage usually easy)
Effect (success w/ vs w/o, trials): Square MH: BC 0% vs BC-RNN 2% success (50 trials each). Square PH: BC 70% vs BC-RNN 80%.

Mechanism (cause→failure): Camera loss → catastrophic drop; training for loss recovers. Interrupting a camera stream mid-rollout removes most policy successes; training with MINT (data augmentation + predictors) recovers much of that loss.
Intervention (category): Training: Fine-tuning on missing-views (MINT) vs none
Paper (title, first author, year, arXiv/: Learning to Act under Visual Interruptions with VLA Models, Jiang et al. 2026 (arXiv:2609.35003)
Effect (success w/ vs w/o, trials): “Camera loss removes a large share of base policy successes; MINT recovers part of that loss on every role”. (Reported qualitatively; e.g. with wrist camera lost at 30% of rollout, base success drops sharply but rises under MINT.)

Mechanism (cause→failure): No action sequence execution → lower success. Executing only one predicted action per timestep (vs a sequence) reduces success on most tasks (~10–20% drop). (E.g. PegInsertion 80%→55%, Faucet 59%→35%, Door 95%→46%.)
Paper (title, first author, year, arXiv/: Unpacking Individual Components of Diffusion Policy, Yuan et al. 2024 (arXiv:2412.00084)
Effect (success w/ vs w/o, trials): ManiSkill PegInsertion: with seq 80% vs single 55%; ManiSkill TurnFaucet 59%→35%; Adroit Door 95%→46% (100 eval runs). Hammer is the one exception.

Mechanism (cause→failure): No receding-horizon control → fails long tasks. Removing MPC-like control causes large drops on long-horizon tasks (e.g. Relocate 64%→11%, StackCube 99%→88%), but no effect or slight gain on very short tasks.
Paper (title, first author, year, arXiv/: Unpacking Diffusion Policy, Yuan et al. 2024
Effect (success w/ vs w/o, trials): Relocate: with 64% vs without 11% (average of 100 trials). StackCube 99%→88%. (Short task Pen: 71%→73%.)

Mechanism (cause→failure): U-Net denoiser vs MLP → success on hard tasks. Using an MLP (no convolutions) for the denoiser causes near-total failure on “hard” tasks. E.g. PegInsertion 80%→21%, Relocate 64%→7%, while “easy” tasks are unaffected.
Paper (title, first author, year, arXiv/: Unpacking Diffusion Policy, Yuan et al. 2024
Effect (success w/ vs w/o, trials): Hard tasks: U-Net 80–64% vs MLP 21–7%. (Easy tasks: 99%→99%, 71%→68%.)

Mechanism (cause→failure): FiLM conditioning vs direct input → large drop. Removing FiLM (using direct observation encoding) greatly reduces success on hard tasks. E.g. PegInsertion 80%→44%, Faucet 59%→27%, Relocate 64%→2%.
Intervention (category): Architecture: FiLM input conditioning (yes vs no)
